biothings.name: hypotonic cerebral palsy
biothings.definition: A type of cerebral palsy characterized by decreased muscle tone. [NCIT:C116906]

biothings.name: athetoid cerebral palsy
biothings.definition: A subtype of cerebral palsy characterized by involuntary, purposeless writhing movements which affect the hands, feet, arms, and legs; the face and tongue may be affected as well, leading to involuntary grimacing, drooling, dysarthria and difficulty eating. [NCIT:C97169]
biothings.synonyms: athetoid cerebral palsy, dyskinetic cerebral palsy

biothings.name: spastic monoplegia
biothings.definition: A spastic cerebral palsy that affects only one limb. [DOID:10968, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_palsy#Ataxic]

biothings.name: ataxic cerebral palsy
biothings.definition: A form of cerebral palsy caused by damage to cerebellar structures. [Wikipedia:Ataxic_cerebral_palsy]

biothings.name: cerebral palsy
biothings.definition: A group of disorders affecting the development of movement and posture, often accompanied by disturbances of sensation, perception, cognition, and behavior. It results from damage to the fetal or infant brain. [NCIT:P378]

opentargets.name: cerebral palsy
opentargets.description: A group of disorders affecting the development of movement and posture, often accompanied by disturbances of sensation, perception, cognition, and behavior. It results from damage to the fetal or infant brain.

opentargets.name: spastic quadriplegic cerebral palsy
opentargets.description: A type of spastic cerebral palsy characterized by increased muscle tone of all four extremities.

opentargets.name: spastic cerebral palsy
opentargets.description: A form of cerebral palsy wherein spasticity is the exclusive impairment present.

opentargets.name: ataxic cerebral palsy
opentargets.description: A form of cerebral palsy caused by damage to cerebellar structures.

opentargets.name: palsy
opentargets.description: A general term most often used to describe severe or complete loss of muscle strength due to motor system disease from the level of the cerebral cortex to the muscle fiber. This term may also occasionally refer to a loss of sensory function. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p45)
